cb7efd7b-9da6-4dc8-be76-3c7e69bdb02e: Y562 is a loose ripe pu’er from Yunnan that drinkers nicknamed the little black box after its export carton. A tiger coming down a hillside appears on the Jixing mark. This lot is dated 1993.
dddd11d2-7357-4d91-86e8-52a99bb47c51: Naka is a village in Mengsong, one of Menghai County’s tea-growing areas. This tea is a ripe pu’er pressed into a cake.
dfb90ef0-fe35-4bc2-a1c5-17084f1f66d4: This ripe pu’er cake comes from the Yiwu tea area of Yunnan. Its recorded year is 2008.
28436463-2272-4f68-83e1-b6d86f798be2: This ripe pu’er brick is from Yunnan and dates to 1990. Ripe pu’er gets its character from wet piling, a process in which damp tea leaves ferment before the tea is dried.
2205c8f5-bcc9-4ec2-823b-fecf68db56fb: This ripe pu’er cake dates to 2015 and is listed as Pasha, Menghai. As ripe pu’er rests, the air and moisture around the leaves shape how its aroma develops.
bb692acb-b4a0-4114-afa8-c9644140eb5f: This loose ripe pu’er comes from the highlands of northern Vietnam, near the Yunnan border. Ripe pu’er is made by fermenting tea leaves in a damp pile, a process called wet piling.
e5e7c9ec-d66b-48de-9197-272ffdb638e0: Xiniu Tang (犀牛塘) means “Rhinoceros Pond.” This tea is a ripe pu’er pressed into a cake.
